subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Which background caller should be the first supported delayed Batch API path, and what provider/runtime lifecycle should it expose?
rationale: This crosses the public provider/runtime boundary and multiple caller surfaces, so an automated implementation cannot safely choose the API, compatibility policy, or fallback behavior.

options.title: Start with isolated cron turns
options.body: Add one additive delayed-turn contract for isolated cron agent turns, including polling, cancellation, accounting, and normal delivery, before considering other callers.

options.title: Design all background callers first
options.body: Specify one lifecycle that covers cron, session sends, subagents, and heartbeats before any provider implementation lands.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep immediate execution as the only core behavior until this cost-optimization feature has explicit maintainer sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Start with isolated cron turns
recommendation.body: Add one additive delayed-turn contract for isolated cron agent turns, including polling, cancellation, accounting, and normal delivery, before considering other callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and provider/cron feature history provide the strongest routing signal for the contract decision.
